At <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> it is at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(4, 2)</annotation></semantics></math>, and it moves up next: counterclockwise.

This ellipse is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> across and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> up and down, taller than wide.

This starts at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 4)</annotation></semantics></math>, the top, and goes clockwise.

Multiply by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a = 3</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, not by their squares.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1 + 3\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 2 + 2\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = 4</annotation></semantics></math>: the top of the ellipse.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(4, 2)</annotation></semantics></math> is the start, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-2, 2)</annotation></semantics></math> is at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = \pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 0)</annotation></semantics></math> is the bottom, at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = \frac{3\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos t = \frac{x - 1}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin t = \frac{y - 2}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>; squaring and adding gives <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{(x - 1)^2}{9} + \frac{(y - 2)^2}{4}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\frac{x - 1}{3}\right)^2</annotation></semantics></math> has <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9</annotation></semantics></math> underneath.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^2 t + \sin^2 t = 1</annotation></semantics></math> is a sum: an ellipse, not a hyperbola.

why.correct: At <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> it is still <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(4, 2)</annotation></semantics></math>, but <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 2 - 2\sin t</annotation></semantics></math> decreases first, so the point heads down: clockwise.
options: Same start, moving down first.

This starts at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-2, 2)</annotation></semantics></math>, the other end.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> still increases, from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2\pi</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>, so the trip is still counterclockwise.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec t = \frac{x}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>y</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan t = \frac{y}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sec</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>tan</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec^2 t - \tan^2 t = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^2}{4} - \frac{y^2}{9} = 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Check <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2\sqrt{2}, 3)</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{8}{4} - \frac{9}{9} = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: The identity <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sec</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>tan</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec^2 t - \tan^2 t = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(4, 3\sqrt{3})</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 + 3 = 7</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>.

Square <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>: the denominators are <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 0)</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> here; the <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> term is the positive one.

why.correct: On this interval <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos t > 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec t \ge 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2\sec t \ge 2</annotation></semantics></math>. The left branch needs <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec t \le -1</annotation></semantics></math>, which happens for <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{2} < t < \frac{3\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> is never negative on this interval.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 3\tan t</annotation></semantics></math> takes negative values too, as the table shows.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> goes <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-3\sqrt{3}, -3, 0, 3, 3\sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math>: it increases, so the point moves up. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> falls to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> and then rises again.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> increases in the table, so the point rises.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> decreases before <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: With <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x}{2} = \sec t</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>y</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{y}{3} = \tan t</annotation></semantics></math>, the identity <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sec</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>tan</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec^2 t - \tan^2 t = 1</annotation></semantics></math> becomes <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^2}{4} - \frac{y^2}{9} = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

This is a definition; it does not link <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>.
